chunks: RLC circuit analysis basics. The question: Basic RLC circuit analysis.
An RLC circuit combines a resistor (R), an inductor (L) and a capacitor (C).
The capacitor and the inductor both store energy, and their opposition to current changes with frequency in opposite ways.
In a series RLC circuit, at one special frequency, the resonant frequency, their effects cancel and only the resistor limits the current.
The resistor also decides whether the circuit rings after a sudden change or settles smoothly.
Picture a child on a swing. The swing wants to go back and forth at its own natural rate. That is resonance.
Friction is the resistor: with a lot of friction the swing creeps to rest, and with very little it keeps swinging for many cycles. Pushing at the natural rate builds a big swing.
The capacitor is like the swing at the top of its arc, holding energy as height. The inductor is like the swing at the bottom, holding energy as speed.
Energy trades between them every cycle.
One current flows through all three elements.
The resistor dissipates, the inductor stores energy in its magnetic field (½Li²), and the capacitor stores it in its electric field (½Cv²).
Capacitor / inductor: a capacitor stores charge; an inductor is a coil of wire that resists changes in current. and "What is inductance?"
Frequency: how many times per second a back-and-forth (AC) signal repeats, in hertz (Hz).
Reactance / impedance: a capacitor's or inductor's opposition to AC, in ohms; impedance is the total, including resistance. and "Inductor impedance equation".
Damping: how quickly the ringing dies out. Q (quality factor): how sharp the resonance is. High Q means little damping.
Take a series circuit with 20 ohms, 1 millihenries and 1 microfarads. It resonates at f 0 equals 1 over (2 pi square root of LC ) , about 5 kilohertz.
